findings.title: SpecialDisplayStats dereferences statOffsets[i].stat / statFactors[i].stat without the null guard used everywhere else
findings.detail: WearerOffset (CompEntad.cs ~line 186) and ClearStatCaches (line 232) both skip null stats, and EntadTraitDef.ConfigErrors (EntadTraitDef.cs:401/403) reports a null stat but the def still loads and can still be rolled. In SpecialDisplayStats the loops call s.LabelCap and s.toStringStyle on an unchecked s, so a trait def that already fails ConfigErrors throws an NRE every time that item's info card opens. Add `if (s == null) continue;` in both display loops.

findings.title: Item card 'Final value' still includes hidden entad statFactors on the def's own equipped offset
findings.detail: On an entad item's card, the equipped-offset row (ThingDef.cs:2418) calls StatOffsetFromGear, which runs stat.parts over the def's equippedStatOffset. StatPart_Entad.TransformValue only skips unrevealed traits when displayExcludesHidden is set (StatPart_Entad.cs:20,26), and that is false here. So a hidden statFactor on that wearer stat is multiplied into the number, while ExplanationPart (StatPart_Entad.cs:63) leaves the factor's line out. That is the same giveaway the buildingGearCard flag fixes for offsets. A narrow fix that keeps caches safe: in StatPart_Entad.TransformValue, set skipHidden = displayExcludesHidden || (EntadWearerStats.buildingGearCard && offsetsViaWearer). The item stats the card reads through GetStatValue (warmup, range and damage multipliers) are not wearer stats, so they still apply hidden factors and their cached values stay correct.

findings.title: AddTrait/RemoveTrait don't clear the holder's stat caches for the added/removed trait's stats
findings.detail: TraitsChanged nulls wearerOffsets but doesn't call ClearStatCaches. ClearStatCaches only runs on the MaxHitPoints path, and on RemoveTrait it runs after the trait has left activeTraits, so that trait's stats are never cleared. StatWorker.GetValue writes temporaryStatCache on every call (StatWorker.cs:35-68), so a caller passing cacheStaleAfterTicks can see the old wearer value until that window runs out. The values are only stale for a short time, never wrong for good.

findings.title: wearerOffsets is published before it is filled
findings.detail: The dictionary is assigned to the field before the loop over activeTraits runs. If anything in the loop throws, a half-built cache stays in place until the next RevealedChanged or TraitsChanged. Building it in a local and assigning it at the end avoids that. This is my opinion only: I have no observed failure.

findings.title: buildingGearCard covers the whole SpecialDisplayStats iterator, including other mods' CompProperties rows
findings.detail: WithGearCard sets the flag around every MoveNext, so it is also set while comps[i].SpecialDisplayStats(req) runs for any mod's CompProperties on the def. If one of those computed a stat for the holder pawn, StatWorker.GetValue would write that pawn's temporaryStatCache (created for every non-immutable stat, StatWorker.cs:31) with the hidden offset left out. A caller using cacheStaleAfterTicks could then read it for a few ticks. Vanilla has no such path, and no fetched corpus mod overrides SpecialDisplayStats(StatRequest). If you want to close it anyway, store the card's Thing instead of a bool and apply the postfix only when gear is that Thing.

findings.title: GearAffectsStat answers per def, so two worn items of one def are both listed if either has a visible offset
findings.detail: PawnHasVisibleEntadOffset returns true if any held item of gearDef has a revealed offset. Vanilla then prints InfoTextLineFromGear for every item of that def, so a second copy with no revealed entad offset still gets a line (+0.00, or showing only its vanilla offset). This is a rare case (duplicate entad defs on one pawn) and cosmetic only.
